A supplier invoice (ref INV-48812) assigned to your cost centre is about to lapse. I need you to confirm you are the approver so I can release it.
explanation: A believable business story plus a deadline pushes you to skip the process that would expose it. The off-domain sender is the giveaway.
red_flags: Sender domain 'northstar-pay.example' is not the company domain 'northstar.example'

subject: Text message
message: Northstar IT: your VPN token expires in 15 minutes. Re-enter your login at northstar-vpn-renew.example/s to keep access. Act now or you will be locked out for 3 days. Do NOT contact the helpdesk, they are overloaded.
explanation: The request (enter your login) is hidden behind a countdown. Real credential renewals never ask you to type a password into a link from a text.
red_flags: The link domain is not the company's, and IT does not collect logins via text links
Threat of lockout to rush you

subject: Call transcript
message: Caller: 'This is Dennis from the payments team, calling again. The wire goes out in ten minutes and I still need your sign-off. If you hang up and call back we will miss the window. Just read me your authoriser PIN and we are done.'
explanation: After earlier contact, the pressure is turned up. Stopping you from independently calling back is the scammer's most important move.
red_flags: Nobody named Dennis appears on the payments team roster, and you never signed off on this wire
Discourages you from calling back on a known number
Asks for approval credentials verbally
